How to install Windows 10 without logging into a Microsoft account

There was a ton of discussion here yesterday about the inherent insecurity of Windows 10 when defaults were left in place.

Following this process leaves the vast majority of those defaults turned off, as most of them rely on Microsoft hooking into your OS by connecting most of the things you do to their web-based services.

I've also seen it argued that their EULA grants them access to everything on your hard drive, even if you don't sign in to an MS account.

There are a couple big problems with that assumption, first one being that in the damning snippets of the EULA that have been posted, MS is describing services, which has a specific meaning in tech, and that is things that run on servers. Cortana is a service, Outlook.com is a service, OneDrive or Skydrive is a service, they all run on and upload data to Microsoft servers. When you connect these services to your PC, Microsoft's terms state that they're able to access that data for the reasons described.

The second is that there would need to be a mechanism for them to do that. Them pulling data off of their servers is easy and almost every web based service has similar terms in their EULA as well. Them pulling files directly from your hard drive that aren't set to sync with their servers is quite a different matter. They'd need to have some kind of file transfer direct to them running, and that would be unacceptable to the vast majority of their customers.

Remember, MS is the leader of the OS market mostly because it dominates the corporate and government world, and having that big of a back door would DEFINITELY be something they wouldn't leave to ambiguity, or they'd be opening themselves to all manner of seriously hot water.

So as far as I can tell, the EULA does not cover them accessing your data if you're not signing in with an MS account and not connecting to those services.

The data you give to Microsoft's servers is accessible by them. The data that you don't, to the best of my research, isn't. While the way they've made everything connect by default and tried to obscure the way to avoid that is definitely shady, by following this step you should be able to stop most of it before it starts.

Cortana is a service, Outlook.com is a service, OneDrive or Skydrive is a service, they all run on and upload data to Microsoft servers.

The big problem is by signing up to those services, you sell your soul to the devil. The big problem is that Microsoft tricks you in this contract. It is the tech unsavy that gets tricked in to this.

Cortana is a huge security and privacy risk, and all you get in return is a lousy talking computer. Cortana is of no use on typical laptops, desktop and tablets. Cortana is only useful on smartphones.

The good news is that the tech unsavy people are education themselves and now know how to remove these settings that are threats to privacy. So these default settings have now even become useless and bad PR.
